meta_title: Alexandre Junior, software engineer for SAP BTP and the web
meta_description: Full-stack software engineer in São Paulo. Five years building on SAP BTP, React, Node and AWS for Whirlpool, Gerdau, Braskem and five other enterprise clients.

hero_lead: I am Alexandre Junior, a full-stack engineer in São Paulo, with five years building software: Fiori, CAP and integrations on SAP BTP, and React, Next.js, NestJS and Python on AWS.
stat_years: years building software that runs in production
stat_clients: enterprise clients, from Whirlpool to Braskem
stat_users: users on the largest platform I worked on
case_optimus_intro: The system that prices the home appliances sold in Brazil under the Electrolux, Brastemp and Consul brands.
case_optimus_work: I worked on it for the whole year: cash and instalment pricing, improvements to the pricing calculations, and the integration with VTEX.
case_apis_intro: Three clients wanted the same thing: new APIs on SAP API Management without building each one by hand. I worked on all three solutions, and each took a different shape.
case_apis_gerdau_text: A Jira card with the API settings was enough. A Python automation read the card and created the API in SAP API Management. I built features for that automation.
case_apis_rhi_text: A React and Node application where the client builds and manages its own APIs, attaches the policies that already exist in API Management and sends each request through an approval queue modelled on GitHub reviews. Creating a new API became 90% more efficient, and the project was presented as a success case in 2024.
case_apis_bunge_text: No interface for the request at all. The client sends a payload, a CI/CD pipeline runs the code that generates the API, and a UI5 app shows metrics for everything that happens.
case_braskem_intro: Moving the applications of an ECC Fiori Launchpad to SAP BTP. Most move as they are. Some I rebuild from scratch, because the originals were written in Web Dynpro for Java.
case_braskem_work: SAP DMS replaces the RFCs that stored files in ECC, called straight from UI5 in the simple cases and through CAP where there is more logic. CAP also reads the signed-in user and shapes each response to the roles defined in BTP Role Collections.
case_advisor_title: An AI advisor for SAP solutions
case_advisor_intro: A UI5 form where someone describes what their application needs. The answers go to a Python backend loaded with SAP content, and a GPT model returns the solution that fits best.
case_advisor_work: The project took second place at SAP Hack2Build 2024.
stack_note: Most of my projects use both: an SAP system on one side, a web product or a cloud service on the other.
client_whirlpool: Optimus Pricing. A payment slip portal I took from pre-sales to delivery, on React, Node and serverless AWS. Support for UI5 applications.
client_gerdau: A Python automation that creates APIs from Jira cards. A Backstage portal that catalogues APIs, ADRs and Kafka files.
client_rhi: A React and Node application for self-service APIs on SAP API Management.
client_bunge: API generation through a CI/CD pipeline, with a UI5 app for metrics.
client_braskem: Migration of ECC Launchpad applications to SAP BTP with UI5, CAP and DMS.
client_piracanjuba: An AI advisor for SAP solutions, awarded at SAP Hack2Build 2024.
client_zilor: Improvements to an application built in SAP Build Apps.
client_bemol: New features for an application built in SAP Build Apps.
about_bio: I started in 2021, building web applications with React, Vue and Python. Since 2022 I have worked on enterprise projects, from APIs and integrations to complete products on SAP BTP and on AWS. I like taking a hard technical problem from planning all the way to production.
